answer: LINE(1st) alone does not achieve the best result by itself; rather, the best Wikipedia page classification performance is obtained when the embeddings learned by LINE(1st) are concatenated with those from LINE(2nd). The reason is that the two objectives capture complementary information: LINE(1st) preserves first-order proximity, meaning it keeps directly connected nodes close in the embedding space, while LINE(2nd) preserves second-order proximity, meaning it captures similarity in neighborhood structure. When combined, the concatenated representation contains both local edge-level similarity and broader structural/contextual similarity, which improves classification accuracy over either embedding alone.
